references.text: The same chapter describes the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, using the same expressions 'ריח ניחוח' (pleasing aroma) and 'אשה ליהוה' (an offering made by fire to the Lord).
The instructions for the burnt offering in Leviticus use the same terminology about burning the sacrifice on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The grain offering is to be burned on the altar as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord, using the same language as in Exodus 29:25.
The peace offering is burned on the altar together with the burnt offering as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The parallel account of the consecration of the priests in Leviticus, where Moses takes the pieces from their hands and burns them on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
The first time the expression 'ריח ניחוח' (pleasing aroma) is used in the Bible, when the Lord smelled the pleasing fragrance from Noah's offering.
Instructions about offerings made by fire to the Lord as a pleasing aroma, whether burnt offerings or fellowship offerings.
Paul uses the same sacrificial terminology regarding Christ's sacrifice: 'εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας' (as a pleasing aroma), as the fulfillment of the Old Testament sacrificial system.
Paul describes the Philippians' gift as 'ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, θυσίαν δεκτήν' (a pleasing aroma, an acceptable sacrifice), alluding to Old Testament sacrificial language.
